title: Warren Collection Opens in Salem With Annabelle Doll and 1,000 Haunted Objects
excerpt: Objects associated with a famous occult museum created by late paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren are now on display in Salem, Massachusetts. The Haunted Warren Museum features these objects...
content:
Objects associated with a famous occult museum created by late paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren are now on display in Salem, Massachusetts. 

The Haunted Warren Museum features these objects as well as Annabelle, considered the scariest doll in the world.

The museum contents and different modes of viewing it will be on display at 259 Essex St. in Salem, according to a Facebook post. These objects will be on exhibition until Christmas.

“For the first time in history, the legendary collection of Ed & Lorraine Warren's Occult Museum has found a public home — giving you the unprecedented opportunity to stand face-to-face with some of the world's most infamous paranormal artifacts,” the Facebook post stated. “Encounter the real Annabelle and explore more than 1,000 authentic haunted objects, cursed artifacts, occult relics, true crime evidence, and historical treasures from around the world.”

Admission starts at $49.99.

According to the Courant, Annabelle is portrayed as a Raggedy Ann doll said to be inhabited by an “inhuman spirit” and historically linked to dangerous or ominous events during its transport and related investigations.

Paranormal fans are so convinced of the doll's evil powers that they feared for Rife's safety when the acquisition was announced.

Other highlights of the museum include Ouija boards, Voodoo dolls, objects used in satanic rituals, a coffin that a 17-year-old boy allegedly occupied before stalking women at night, and artifacts from a plane that crashed into the Florida Everglades, according to the Courant.
